clean_room: All minor-body data come from JPL. Swiss Ephemeris is used only as a black-box oracle in harness/check_minor.py, never as a data source.

sb441.how_read: HTTP Range requests, 1 MiB chunk cache (data/sources/minor/sb441-n16_cache)
sb441.integrity: not hashed (range-read); DAF/type-2 directory checks in tools/spk.py, record grid checked, record-boundary continuity <= 3e-7 km
sb441.kind: JPL DE441 small-body perturber SPK (type 2, Chebyshev, 32-day records)
sb441.reference: Park, Folkner, Williams, Boggs (2021), JPL IOM 392R-21-005; DE440/DE441 paper AJ 161:105
sb441.note: Asteroid trajectories integrated simultaneously with the DE441 planets (the same ones used as perturbers in DE441 and in every Horizons small-body integration).
sb441.license: JPL Solar System Dynamics data (NASA/JPL-Caltech). No licence terms are attached to the files; JPL asks for credit to the Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System / SSD group. The Horizons SPK comments state the files are informal releases, not for spacecraft-safety use. Confirm the attribution wording with JPL SSD before public redistribution of derived packs.

horizons.force_model: planets, Moon, 16 largest asteroids (SB441-N16), PPN solar relativity, Earth oblateness, non-gravitational terms of the solution (from the SPK comments)
horizons.horizons_span_limit: Horizons refuses ephemerides for this body before A.D. 1599-DEC-11 TDB ('No ephemeris for target ... prior to'), so no JPL data exists before
